title: SemStruct: Contextualizing Semantic Embeddings with Structural Information for Schema Matching

problem.claim: Heterogeneous data integration requires aligning schemas across sources.

gap.claim: Serialized-text processing by pretrained language models discards row-level co-occurrence and relational context, leaving models reliant on column-header semantics or standalone distributions.

contributions.claim: SemStruct joins frozen pretrained language models with the structural inductive bias of graph neural networks.
SemStruct models tables as heterogeneous graphs with columns and values as nodes connected by rows, enabling structural context propagation.
The framework freezes the language model and trains only a lightweight structural encoder.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On the Valentine and SOTAB-SM benchmarks, the authors report state-of-the-art performance and say SemStruct outperforms fully fine-tuned baselines on complex, semantically joinable datasets.
The authors report that ablation studies identify row representations primarily as topological conduits rather than semantic entities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Schema matching supports integration of heterogeneous data sources.
Serialized tabular representations used by pretrained language models lose row-level relational context.
SemStruct combines frozen language-model semantics with graph neural network structure and represents tables as heterogeneous graphs.
The language model remains frozen while only a lightweight structural encoder is trained.
The authors report benchmark gains and ablation findings supporting explicit structural modeling.
